title: versions/<versionId>/package.json and extras/<extraId>/package.json — what the packager produced
description:
Written once by the packager, when the package completes, and never touched again. It sits next to the bytes it describes, so it can never end up describing a different package, and it is the record a rebuild reads to restore the playback rows: everything the v1 manifest's playback section carried is here, under the same names.

An extra's package (extras/<extraId>/, see extra.schema.json) is described by this same record, with two differences. Its checksums.sha256 lists extra.json, the extra's originals and every package file — an extra is written whole and no event deletes its original — and it carries no trailers: a trailer that is a file of its own is an extra of kind trailer.

Because it is written only on completion, there is no 'building' or 'failed' state to record — an unfinished package has no package.json and no .complete marker, and neither the database nor a rebuild will use it. A package that falls out of date later is not rewritten either: a new version folder holds the new package, and an events/…-package-superseded.json record says this one was replaced.

The records a rebuild trusts are covered by one chain, each link written after the one it covers:
  .complete         written last; holds 'sha256:<hex>' of this file, and nothing else
  package.json      this file; checksums.sha256 records the hash of the checksums file
  checksums.sha256  version.json and every file of the package, sha256sum -c format
so `sha256sum -c checksums.sha256` proves version.json and the package, the hash here proves the checksums file, and .complete proves this file. The checksums file cannot list .complete, this file or itself — each holds the hash of the next link down — and it does not list the originals, which are covered by their source records' fixity and may be deleted later.

Paths: renditions[].dir, subtitles[].path, subtitles[].hls, trickplay.vttPath, hls.master, trailers[].manifestPath and checksums.file are relative to the version or extra folder THIS record sits in. subtitles[].fromSidecar is the one path relative to the ITEM folder: it names the copy a source folder keeps of the sidecar the subtitle was made from.

createdAt.description: When the package completed. This is the v1 playback field packagedAt under the name every v2 record uses.

state.description: 'complete': finished and playable, and the version folder carries its .complete marker, which names this file's hash. 'stale' exists only for a record migrated from a v1 manifest that already said the package was outdated; nothing writes it now, because a package that goes out of date gets a package-superseded event instead of a new state here.

role.description: What this package was when it was written: 'derived' when an original was kept beside it in its folder, 'canonical' when the package is the only copy. It is not rewritten when the original is deleted later — a reader that sees an original-deleted event for this version treats the package as canonical from then on, and every loss below becomes permanent.

durationMs.description: v1 playback field: duration of this package.

recipe.description: How video, audio and subtitles were produced, so the same package can be made again.

renditions.description: v1 playback field. More than one video entry is a quality ladder.

audio.description: One stereo rendition per audio track of the original the package carries, in the playlist's stereo group.

audioSurround.description: The 5.1 companions of tracks the stereo renditions also carry, in an audio group of their own: the original's own surround stream, copied, or one encode of it. A track is listed once under audio whatever it has here, so a reader counts tracks there and channels in both.

hls.description: How the package is laid out as HLS, as the packager wrote it: the master playlist a player opens, the length its media segments are cut to, the audio groups the master names — the stereo one and, with 5.1 companions, theirs — and the subtitle group, or null when the master names no subtitles.

trailers.description: v1 playback field: trailers packaged into this folder. Trailers published elsewhere are listed by reference in metadata.json, and a trailer that is a local file of its own is an extra of kind trailer (extras/<extraId>/), not one of these.

sizeBytes.description: Total size of the package's files: its rendition, subtitle, trickplay and trailer folders, not the records beside them.

peakBandwidthBps.description: The highest BANDWIDTH in the package's master playlist, audio included: a peak, not an average. The rendition field bitrateBps is often 0.

losses.description: Every way the package is poorer than the original. Empty only when lossless.

essence.description: What this package carries, in the same reduced terms as the source's, so the two can be compared. What the originals would cost to delete is not here but on the version, which can answer it whether or not anything has been packaged.

checksums.description: A sha256sum-style file listing version.json and every file of the package — the rendition, subtitle, trickplay and trailer folders — so a copy can be verified file by file; in an extra's folder, extra.json, the originals and every file of the package. It is written with the package, not later: once the original is gone the package is the truth, and this is its fixity.

file.description: In this version folder: lines of '<hex digest>  <path>', paths relative to this folder.

sha256.description: Hash of the checksums file itself: the link from this record down to the files it lists.

files.description: How many files it lists, version.json included — or extra.json and the originals, in an extra's folder.

bytes.description: Their total size, the same files included.

sourceStreamIndex.description: The original's stream this was made from.

peakBitrateBps.description: The highest bitrate of any segment of the rendition, where bitrateBps is the average.

videoRange.description: The VIDEO-RANGE the master playlist gives the rendition.

label.description: The rung's name in the ladder, e.g. 'source', '1080p'.

encoder.description: What made the rung: 'copy' when it is the original's own stream, otherwise the encoder.

default.description: What the packager wrote into the playlist, so a reader sees the package as it is. Which track a viewer actually gets is behaviour and comes from the database.

visible.description: As written into the playlist; see default.

sourceChannels.description: Channels of the original track, e.g. 6 when a 5.1 track was downmixed to stereo.

original.description: True when the file flagged the track as the work's original language; null when unknown.

group.description: The HLS audio group the rendition is in, one hls.audioGroups names.

name.description: The NAME the master playlist gives the rendition.

default.description: As written into the playlist; see the audio rendition's default.

forced.description: As written into the playlist. The content fact is purpose 'forced'.

name.description: The NAME the master playlist gives the subtitle's HLS rendition.

hls.description: The folder of the subtitle's HLS rendition, when it was segmented into one.

fromSidecar.description: The subtitle was made from a sidecar that sat beside the original, and this is the copy of it the source folder keeps: sources/<sourceId>/<name>, relative to the item folder — of a source this version was made from, and one its source.json lists among its sidecars. An extra has no source record, so no subtitle of an extra's package carries it.

trickplay.description: The VTT maps each interval to one cell of one sprite sheet.
